prompt.text:
Your task is to generate a complete research paper using the materials below.
You must produce:
1. A BibTeX bibliography file (references.bib)
2. The full LaTeX paper (template.tex)

Instructions
• Use the research idea and experimental logs to construct a coherent, rigorous ML paper.
• For related work and baselines:
  – Search for and include influential papers published up until 2024-11.
  – Incorporate relevant literature and add the corresponding BibTeX entries to references.bib.
  – Do NOT hallucinate papers or reference keys; all citation entries must be real.
• In the LaTeX paper, cite papers using \cite{} with keys that match exactly with your entries in references.bib.
• Do not fabricate experimental results or make claims unsupported by the logs.

Materials
Here are all the raw research materials to assist with the writing process:

[RESEARCH IDEA]
## Problem Statement
Current self-supervised Structure-from-Motion (SfM) approaches rely heavily on photometric consistency, which requires rich textures and distinct gradient variations to establish reliable correspondence between frames. This paradigm breaks down significantly in indoor environments characterized by large, low-texture regions (e.g., white walls, ceilings, and floors). In these "flat" regions, photometric error remains low even when depth estimation is grossly inaccurate, leading to infinite or random depth predictions. Existing methods fail to leverage illumination cues that could define shape in the absence of texture.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose that the ambiguity of textureless regions can be resolved by coupling **Structure-from-Motion (SfM)** with **Shape-from-Shading (SfS)**. We hypothesize that while texture drives motion estimation, shading intensity provides the necessary constraints for surface shape recovery in uniform areas. By simultaneously learning inverse rendering (decomposing images into albedo and shading) and geometric reconstruction, we can utilize shading information to optimize the scene shape estimated by SfM. We believe that enforcing consistency between the geometric structures derived from motion and the surface normals derived from shading will prevent the collapse of depth estimation in textureless zones.

## Proposed Methodology (High-Level Technical Approach)

We propose a dual-pathway self-supervised framework: a **Shape-from-Shading (SfS) Pathway** and a **Structure-from-Motion (SfM) Pathway**. These pathways will be trained jointly using a set of novel mutual consistency constraints.

**1. Dual-Pathway Architecture:**
*   **SfS Pathway (Inverse Rendering):** We will design a network to decompose a single frame into Albedo and Surface Normals. From these, we will infer Shading and Light sources to reconstruct the original image. This reconstruction loss acts as the primary self-supervision for the shading component.
*   **SfM Pathway (Geometry):** A parallel network will take image sequences as input to predict dense Depth maps and Camera Motion (Pose).

**2. Bridging Constraints (The "Glue"):**
To overcome the textureless problem, we will introduce specific constraints that link these two pathways:

*   **Keypoint-Focused Photometric Consistency:** Instead of applying photometric loss to all pixels (which causes errors in flat regions), we will restrict the temporal consistency loss to extracted keypoints (edges and corners). This ensures the motion estimation relies only on reliable features.
*   **Surface Shape Consistency (Cross-Task):** We will enforce geometric consistency between the **Depth** predicted by the SfM pathway and the **Normals** predicted by the SfS pathway. By deriving normals from the SfM depth map and comparing them to the SfS normals, we can force the depth map to respect the curvature implied by shading.
*   **3D Scene Registration:** We will treat the outputs of both networks as 3D point clouds. We propose a registration loss that minimizes the spatial distance between the point cloud generated by SfM and the point cloud implied by the SfS network. This acts as a global geometric constraint.
*   **Layout Consistency:** We will incorporate a room layout estimator to detect structural lines (e.g., wall-floor boundaries). We will force the 3D reconstruction, when back-projected, to align with these detected 2D layout lines, anchoring the geometry to the room's physical structure.

**3. Adaptive Brightness:**
To handle lighting variations between frames, we will model brightness changes explicitly with learnable parameters, preventing lighting shifts from being misinterpreted as geometric motion.

## Expected Contribution
*   **Theoretical Novelty:** A unified framework that explicitly bridges the gap between inverse rendering (shading/albedo) and geometric reconstruction (SfM) in a fully unsupervised manner.
*   **Robustness in Textureless Scenes:** By substituting texture constraints with shading and layout constraints, we expect to solve the "infinite depth" artifact common in indoor self-supervised learning.
*   **Holistic Scene Understanding:** The model will yield not just depth and pose, but also intrinsic image components (Albedo, Normals, Shading) without requiring ground-truth labels.

[EXPERIMENTAL LOGS]
## 1. Experimental Setup

*   **Datasets:**
    *   **NYUv2 Depth Dataset (Indoor):** Comprised 582 indoor video sequences. We selected 283 scenes for the training split and used the official testing split from another 25 scenes for evaluation. Training images were sampled every ten frames to reduce redundancy. We applied a fixed 3-frame length in the Structure-from-Motion (SfM) network.
    *   **ScanNet (Indoor):** A large indoor dataset with 1513 video sequences (approximately 2.5 million images). Used for evaluation and generalization testing.
    *   **FinnForest (Outdoor):** Used sequences in winter conditions containing texture-less pathways covered with snow to test generalization.
*   **Evaluation Metrics:**
    *   **Error Metrics:** Absolute Relative Error (AbsRel), Root Mean Squared Error (RMS), Log10 Error.
    *   **Accuracy Metrics:** $\delta_1$ ($\delta < 1.25$), $\delta_2$ ($\delta < 1.25^2$), $\delta_3$ ($\delta < 1.25^3$).
*   **Baselines Compared:**
    *   **Supervised Methods:** Wang et al., Eigen et al., Liu et al., Li et al., Xu et al., DORN, SharpNet, Adabins, P3Depth, NeWCRFs, Trap Attention.
    *   **Unsupervised Methods:** GeoNet, SC-SfMLearner, Monodepth2, MovingIndoor, TrianFlow, PackNet-SfM, Johnston et al., P²Net (3-frame), HR-Depth, Lite-Mono, RA-Depth.
*   **Implementation Details:**
    *   **Architecture:** Encoder-decoder structure using ResNet-18 (pre-trained on ImageNet) for both the SfM-Net and SfS-Net (Shape-from-Shading) pathways.
    *   **Input Resolution:** Indoor images resized to $640 \times 480$; outdoor images resized to $512 \times 256$ for training.
    *   **Hyperparameters (Loss Weights):**
        *   Shading Reconstruction ($L_{shading\_rec}$): 1.0
        *   Spectral Consistency ($L_{spectral}$): 1.0
        *   Layout Consistency ($L_{layout}$): 0.5
        *   Geometric Consistency ($L_{geo}$): 0.5
        *   Smoothness ($L_{smooth}$): 0.1
        *   Surface Shape ($L_{surface\_shape}$): 0.2
        *   Scene Registration ($L_{scene\_reg}$): 0.2
    *   **Optimizer:** Adam optimizer with $\beta_1 = 0.9$, $\beta_2 = 0.99$, and weight decay $5 \times 10^{-4}$.
    *   **Training Schedule:** Trained for a total of 50 epochs. Initial learning rate of $1e^{-4}$ for the first 20 epochs, gradually reduced to half for the remaining epochs.

## 3. Qualitative Observations

*   **3D Reconstruction Quality (NYUv2 & ScanNet):**
    *   We observed that the proposed method prevented stretching and distortion effects in the generated point clouds that were present in results from comparable methods.
    *   These improvements were specifically notable on uniform and low-textured surfaces.
*   **Albedo and Shading Decomposition:**
    *   The method produced high-quality decompositions of albedo and shading in an unsupervised manner.
    *   When compared to other approaches, our shading network achieved superior visual results, such as better recovery of wall albedo and bed shading features.
*   **Generalization to Outdoor Scenes (FinnForest):**
    *   Although the model was targeted at indoor scenes, we observed stable and accurate albedo and shading map generation when tested on challenging outdoor snow scenes (texture-less pathways).
*   **Cross-Dataset Generalization:**
    *   A network trained exclusively on NYUv2 data generalized well to unseen indoor images from the ScanNet dataset.
    *   The model successfully generated estimated albedo, shading, and normal maps on this unseen data without further training.
*   **Ablation Effects:**
    *   We observed that the progressive addition of Shape-from-Shading (SfS-Net), Surface Shape Consistency (SSC), Scene Registration Consistency (SRC), Keypoint-based Consistency (KPC), and Layout Prediction Consistency (LPC) systematically reduced the AbsRel error and increased the $\delta_1$ accuracy.

prompt.text:
Role: Senior AI Researcher and Academic Writer.
Objective: Complete a machine learning research paper by filling in missing sections of a provided LaTeX template and generating a corresponding bibliography file. You must produce a scientifically sound, well-structured paper suitable for submission to a top-tier ML conference.

Inputs
You will receive the following materials:
• idea.md: Detailed description of the proposed method and technical ideas.
• experimental_log.md: Raw experimental results and observations used to construct tables, figures, and analysis.
• conference_guidelines.md: Formatting and stylistic requirements for the target conference.
• figures_list: A list of figures that may be referenced in the paper.

Conference Guidelines
# CVPR 2025 Paper Writing Guidelines

Below are the instructions to help you with the latex paper writing process for CVPR 2025.

## Language
All manuscripts must be in English.

## Submission Policies & Anonymity
CVPR reviewing is double-blind. Authors must not know the names of the reviewers, and reviewers must not know the names of the authors.

* **No Identifying Information:** Do not provide information that may identify the authors in the acknowledgments (e.g., co-workers and grant IDs) or in the supplementary material.
* **Links:** Do not provide links to websites that identify the authors.
* **GitHub:** Links to GitHub must be anonymous.
* **Self-Citation:** If you need to cite any of your own papers that are being submitted concurrently, include anonymized versions in the supplementary material and cite them as anonymous. Do not use the words "my" or "our" when citing previous work; treat your own prior work as if it were written by someone else (e.g., "Smith et al. showed..." rather than "We showed...").

## Paper length
Papers, excluding the references section, must be no longer than eight pages in length.
The references section will not be included in the page count, and there is no limit on the length of the references section.
For example, a paper of eight pages with two pages of references would have a total length of 10 pages.

Overlength papers, or papers where margins and formatting are deemed significantly altered, will simply not be reviewed.

## Mathematics
Please number all of your sections and displayed equations as in these examples:
```latex
\begin{equation}
  E = m\cdot c^2
  \label{eq:important}
\end{equation}
```
and
```latex
\begin{equation}
  v = a\cdot t.
  \label{eq:also-important}
\end{equation}
```

## Formatting your paper
All text must be in a two-column format.
The total allowable size of the text area is $6\frac78$ inches (17.46 cm) wide by $8\frac78$ inches (22.54 cm) high.
Columns are to be $3\frac14$ inches (8.25 cm) wide, with a $\frac{5}{16}$ inch (0.8 cm) space between them.
The main title (on the first page) should begin 1 inch (2.54 cm) from the top edge of the page.
The second and following pages should begin 1 inch (2.54 cm) from the top edge.
On all pages, the bottom margin should be $1\frac{1}{8}$ inches (2.86 cm) from the bottom edge of the page for $8.5 \times 11$-inch paper;
for A4 paper, approximately $1\frac{5}{8}$ inches (4.13 cm) from the bottom edge of the page.

### Type style and fonts
Wherever Times is specified, Times Roman may also be used. If neither is available on your word processor, please use the font closest in appearance to Times to which you have access.

### Main Title
Center the title $1\frac{3}{8}$ inches (3.49 cm) from the top edge of the first page. The title should be in Times 14-point, boldface type. Capitalize the first letter of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs; do not capitalize articles, coordinate conjunctions, or prepositions (unless the title begins with such a word).

The ABSTRACT and MAIN TEXT are to be in a two-column format.

### Main Text
Type main text in 10-point Times, single-spaced.
Do NOT use double-spacing.
All paragraphs should be indented 1 pica (approx.~$\frac{1}{6}$ inch or 0.422 cm). Make sure your text is fully justified---that is, flush left and flush right. Please do not place any additional blank lines between paragraphs.

Figure and table captions should be 9-point Roman type as in \cref{fig:onecol,fig:short}. 
Short captions should be centred.

\noindent Callouts should be 9-point Helvetica, non-boldface type. Initially capitalize only the first word of section titles and first-, second-, and third-order headings.

#### First-order Headings
For example, {\large \bf 1. Introduction} should be Times 12-point boldface, initially capitalized, flush left, with one blank line before, and one blank line after.

#### Second-order Headings
For example, { \bf 1.1. Database elements} should be Times 11-point boldface, initially capitalized, flush left, with one blank line before, and one after.
If you require a third-order heading (we discourage it), use 10-point Times, boldface, initially capitalized, flush left, preceded by one blank line, followed by a period and your text on the same line.

### Footnotes
Please use \footnote{This is what a footnote looks like.
It often distracts the reader from the main flow of the argument.} sparingly.

Indeed, try to avoid footnotes altogether and include necessary peripheral observations in the text (within parentheses, if you prefer, as in this sentence). If you wish to use a footnote, place it at the bottom of the column on the page on which it is referenced.
Use Times 8-point type, single-spaced.

### Cross-references
For the benefit of author(s) and readers, please use the
```latex
{\small\begin{verbatim}
  \cref{...}
\end{verbatim}}
```
command for cross-referencing to figures, tables, equations, or sections.

This will automatically insert the appropriate label alongside the cross-reference as in this example:
```latex
\begin{quotation}
  To see how our method outperforms previous work, please see \cref{fig:onecol} and \cref{tab:example}.
  It is also possible to refer to multiple targets as once, \eg~to \cref{fig:onecol,fig:short-a}.
  You may also return to \cref{sec:formatting} or look at \cref{eq:also-important}.
\end{quotation}
```
If you do not wish to abbreviate the label, for example at the beginning of the sentence, you can use the
```latex
{\small\begin{verbatim}
  \Cref{...}
\end{verbatim}}
command. Here is an example:
\begin{quotation}
  \Cref{fig:onecol} is also quite important.
\end{quotation}
```

```

    \fbox{\rule{0pt}{2in} \rule{.9\linewidth}{0pt}}
    \caption{An example of a subfigure.}
    \label{fig:short-a}
  \end{subfigure}

    \fbox{\rule{0pt}{2in} \rule{.9\linewidth}{0pt}}
    \caption{Another example of a subfigure.}
    \label{fig:short-b}
  \end{subfigure}
  \caption{Example of a short caption, which should be centered.}
  \label{fig:short}
\end{figure*}
```

## Illustrations, graphs, and photographs
All graphics should be centered.
In \LaTeX, avoid using the \texttt{center} environment for this purpose, as this adds potentially unwanted whitespace.
Instead use
```latex
{\small\begin{verbatim}
  \centering
\end{verbatim}}
```
at the beginning of your figure.

Please ensure that any point you wish to make is resolvable in a printed copy of the paper. Resize fonts in figures to match the font in the body text, and choose line widths that render effectively in print.

When placing figures in \LaTeX, it's almost always best to use \verb+\includegraphics+, and to specify the figure width as a multiple of the line width as in the example below

```latex
{\small\begin{verbatim}
   \usepackage{graphicx} ...
   \includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]
                   {myfile.pdf}
\end{verbatim}}
```

## Color
If you use color in your plots, please keep in mind that a significant subset of reviewers and readers may have a color vision deficiency; red-green blindness is the most frequent kind.
Hence avoid relying only on color as the discriminative feature in plots (such as red \vs green lines), but add a second discriminative feature to ease disambiguation.


## Important Rules 
* DO NOT change `\usepackage[capitalize]{cleveref}` into `\usepackage[capitalize]{cleverref}`, as there's no `cleverref.sty`.
* Keep the existing packages in the template unchanged.
* For consistent compilation across environments, all figures will reside in the `figures` directory. Always include the `figures/` prefix in your `\includegraphics` command. Failing to include this prefix (e.g., using `figure_1.png` instead of `figures/figure_1.png`) will result in figure loading errors during the build process.
* Always use the following author information placeholder in your writeup:
    * Ambitious AI Researcher, AI Research Institute, 123 AI Avenue, ML City, researcher@institute.ai


Critical Constraints
1. Scientific Integrity
• All reported experimental results MUST match the provided experimental logs.
• Never fabricate results, numbers, baselines, datasets, or metrics.
• If results are weak, negative, or inconclusive, report them honestly and discuss possible explanations.
2. Literature Cutoff Rule

references.text:
## Problem Statement
Scene reconstruction in indoor environments presents a unique challenge compared to outdoor scenarios. Standard Structure-from-Motion (SfM) approaches rely heavily on rich textures and distinct gradient variations to establish feature correspondences and photometric constraints. However, indoor scenes frequently contain large, low-texture regions (e.g., white walls, ceilings, floors) and repeated patterns. In these texture-less areas, photometric errors remain close to zero even when estimated depths are infinite or random, leading to a collapse in reconstruction performance.

While Shape-from-Shading (SfS) techniques can recover fine surface details in such regions based on shading cues, they suffer from inherent ambiguity regarding scale and lighting, making them difficult to apply directly to real-world navigation tasks. There is currently no framework that effectively unifies the geometric structure capability of SfM with the detailed surface estimation of SfS to robustly reconstruct texture-less indoor environments in a self-supervised manner.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose a novel framework, **Shading-SfM-Net**, which hypothesizes that the ambiguity of low-texture regions in SfM can be resolved by incorporating inverse rendering constraints from an SfS network. Conversely, the metric ambiguity of SfS can be constrained by the geometric structure learned via SfM.

By simultaneously learning a shape-from-shading network (predicting albedo, normal, and lighting) and a structure-from-motion network (predicting depth and pose), we can leverage mutual information. We predict that enforcing consistency between the surface normals derived from SfM depth and the normals predicted by SfS, alongside layout and keypoint-specific constraints, will enable accurate dense reconstruction of indoor scenes without requiring ground-truth depth labels.

## Proposed Methodology (Detailed Technical Approach)

We will develop an end-to-end deep learning framework comprising two coupled pathways: a Shape-from-Shading (SfS) pathway and a Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pathway.

### 1. Shape-from-Shading (SfS) Pathway
We will design this pathway to perform inverse rendering on a single frame. The network, denoted as $\psi(\cdot)$, will take an image $I$ as input and output the Albedo map $A$, Surface Normal map $N$, Shading map $S$, and Light source $L$.
$$ SfS-Net: \psi(I) \rightarrow \{A, N, S, L\} $$
The shading map $S$ and light source $L$ will be inferred via a second-order spherical harmonics illumination model $f$ using the predicted normals. The reconstructed image $I_{rec}$ is defined as:
$$ I_{rec} = A \cdot S = A \cdot L f(N) $$
where $f(N)$ utilizes the basis $[1, n_x, n_y, n_z, 3n_z^2-1, n_x n_y, n_x n_z, n_y n_z, n_x^2 - n_y^2]^T$.

**Shading Reconstruction Loss:** To drive the learning, we will minimize the reconstruction error between $I_{rec}$ and the raw image $I_{raw}$. Crucially, to handle perceptual uniformity better than RGB, we will compute this loss in the **CIELAB color space**:
$$ L_{shading\_rec} = \left\| LAB(I_{raw}) - LAB(I_{rec}) \right\|_1 $$

### 2. Adaptive SfM Pathway
The SfM pathway will take adjacent frames $I_t$ and $I_{t+1}$ to predict dense depth maps $(D_t, D_{t+1})$ and the relative pose vector $T_{t, t+1}$. We define the inverse projection from pixel $p=(x,y)$ to 3D space as:
$$ \pi^{-1}(p, D(p)) = ((x - c_x)D/f_x, (y - c_y)D/f_y, D, 1) $$
where $f_{x,y}$ and $c_{x,y}$ are focal lengths and principal points. The warping operation $\omega$ to synthesize $I_t$ from $I_{t+1}$ is:
$$ \omega(p, T_{t, t+1}) = \pi(T_{t, t+1} \pi^{-1}(p, D(p))) $$

**Keypoint-Driven Spectral Consistency:**
To prevent the SfM network from learning wrong information from texture-less regions, we will restrict the photometric loss to **BRISK keypoints** $\mathbf{Kp}$. Furthermore, we will model brightness variations using learnable parameters $m$ and $b$ ($I' = m \cdot I + b$). The loss is:
$$ L_{spectral} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i,j} | I'_{t+1}(\omega(\mathbf{Kp}(i,j), T_{t, t+1})) - I'_t(\mathbf{Kp}(i,j)) | $$

**Geometric and Smoothness Constraints:**
We will enforce geometric consistency between the predicted depth $D_t$ and the warped depth $D'_t = D_{t+1}(\omega(p, T))$:
$$ L_{geo} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i,j} | D'_t(\omega(\mathbf{Kp}(i,j), T_{t, t+1})) - D_t(\mathbf{Kp}(i,j)) | $$
We will also include an edge-preserving smoothness term $L_{smooth}$ weighted by image gradients.

**Layout Consistency Constraint:**
To preserve indoor structural integrity (wall-floor boundaries), we will detect 2D line segments $\mathcal{L} = \{ \ell_i \}$ in the input image and align them with lines detected in the back-projected 3D scene. We define a line by endpoints and slope-intercept parameters $(a, b)$. We will minimize the layout loss $L_{layout}$ over matched line pairs $\mathcal{C}$:
$$ L_{layout} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{C}|} \sum_{(\ell^{img}, \ell^{proj}) \in \mathcal{C}} ( \|\text{endpoints diff}\|_1 + \lambda_s |a^{img} - a^{proj}| + \lambda_b |b^{img} - b^{proj}| ) $$

### 3. Joint Optimization (Bridging SfS and SfM)
We propose three specific consistency terms to bridge the two pathways.

**A. Cross-Normal Consistency:**
We will enforce consistency between the normal predicted by SfS ($\tilde{n}$) and the normal derived from the gradient of the SfM depth map ($\tilde{d}$). We formulate this as minimizing the dissimilarity of their directions:
$$ L_{cross-normal} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_i \left( 1 - \frac{< \tilde{d}_i, \tilde{n}_i >}{\| \tilde{d}_i \| \cdot \| \tilde{n}_i \|} \right) $$

**B. Surface Shape Consistency (Curved Surface Fitting):**
We assume texture-less regions (floors, walls) share continuous depth profiles. We will extract superpixel segments from the **SfS-estimated Albedo map**. For points within a segment, we fit a curved surface model $M \in \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $M^T P = [1, \dots, 1]^T$. The loss minimizes the deviation of the SfM-estimated depth from this fitted curved surface:
$$ L_{surface\_shape} = \sum_{m} \sum_{i} | D(p_i) - (M^T K^{-1} p_i)^{-1} | $$

**C. Scene Registration Consistency:**
We will construct 3D point clouds from both the SfS network ($P_{SfS}$) and the SfM network ($P_{SfM}$). We will minimize the Chamfer distance between the transformed point clouds across time frames (registration loss) and the distance between SfS and SfM point clouds at the same timestamp:
$$ L_{scene\_reg} = \sum \| T \cdot P^{t+1}_{SfM} - P^t_{SfS} \|_2^2 + \sum \| P^t_{SfM} - P^t_{SfS} \|_2^2 $$

## Expected Contribution
1.  **Framework Novelty:** We will deliver "Shading-SfM-Net," the first self-supervised architecture to explicitly couple Shape-from-Shading inverse rendering with Structure-from-Motion for indoor scenes.
2.  **Robustness in Texture-less Zones:** By utilizing the proposed **Cross-Normal** and **Surface Shape** consistencies, we expect to solve the infinite/random depth estimation problem in white-walled indoor environments where standard photometric losses fail.
3.  **Geometric Precision:** The introduction of **Layout Consistency** and **Keypoint-Driven** spectral losses will theoretically ensure that dominant indoor structures (Manhattan world assumptions) are preserved without requiring supervised depth labels.
4.  **Generalization:** By disentangling albedo and shading from motion, the system is expected to generalize better to unseen datasets compared to methods that overfit to specific texture distributions.

notes.task_input: Only the `# Goal` and `# Rubrics` sections of task.md are read: all five candidate files are put under `# Goal` with their headings turned into bold lines; `# Rubrics` carries a neutral line. notes.phases: execution.phases=task_drafting,investigation,final_evaluation,paper; the system's own default also runs ablations and posthoc; final_evaluation stays because a drafted task requires it before the paper. review/revision (second model) are never selected.
notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator container has the host docker socket (root-equivalent on the host).

preinstalled.zh: python:3.11 bookworm；上游代码按 PYTHONPATH 使用；pdflatex + bibtex；CPU 版 PyTorch 和 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn、pandas、matplotlib 等（constraints.txt 固定）
preinstalled.en: python:3.11 bookworm; upstream code via PYTHONPATH; pdflatex + bibtex; CPU PyTorch with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib and more (pinned by constraints.txt)

notes.model: claude-opus-5-5 through the Anthropic Messages API (llm.provider=anthropic), no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. Requests carry model, messages and max_tokens only (no tools, no thinking parameter); ARC's per-stage temperature is not sent because the model rejects it, so the API default applies.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain chat completions. conditions.agent=claude means only that the provider is Anthropic; Claude Code is not involved. Generated experiments run as a plain subprocess in the container.
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; usage-log.patch sends output_config.effort='high' with every request. Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and ARC's per-stage max_tokens (for example 4096) is shared with the thinking tokens, so long outputs can still be cut short.
notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. A logging-only patch (usage-log.patch) appends each Messages API `usage` block to anthropic-usage.jsonl; cost is not computed. The same patch carries the RWE_OMIT_TEMPERATURE and RWE_EFFORT switches.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s, refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md verbatim with whitespace collapsed. Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request to api.anthropic.com is built in researchclaw/llm/anthropic_adapter.py:136-148 and carries only model, messages, max_tokens, optional temperature, output_config.effort and system, never a tools or web_search field; the OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter :online / plugins) is not used (llm.provider=anthropic), web_search.enabled=false, Gemini is only used by the disabled figure_agent.nano_banana. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so such a path would be invisible to the audit.
notes.secrets: Generated experiment code inherits the container environment, including the API keys (ARC offers no switch to scrub it).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit.
